title.narrative: Strengthened national policy and institutional environment to promote decent work opportunities and sustainable economic transformation for disadvantaged groups

description.narrative: Mozambique’s economy is heavily reliant on agriculture, resource extraction and primary commodity production. This economic structure creates a situation that combines low productivity and value-added production, with high levels of poverty and inequality. About 70% of employed Mozambicans work in the agricultural sector, however, they only contribute to about 25% of GDP, clearly indicating the deep-seated poverty associated with rural and agrarian settings, disproportionately affecting youth, women and people Living with Disabilities (PWDs) due to their already higher vulnerabilities. Against this context, the CPO is supporting the National Government (Ministry of Land and Environment (MTA), the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, the State Secretary for Youth and Employment, the Ministry of Labour and Social Security, the Ministry of Public Works) and the social partners in the development of a range of interrelated policies, action plans and interventions, promoting: Decent Work in Rural Areas through the development of the regulation of the new Forestry Law, in cooperation with FAO, Youth employment in rural areas through the development of the National Action Plan (PAPE) of the Employment Policy for Rural Youth in Mozambique, focusing on education, finance, land access, and youth participation in decision-making.
